candidates.title: Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces

candidates.abstract: Abstract Anisotropic van der Waals materials exhibit direction-dependent optical and electronic properties, enabling tailored directional light–matter interactions. Rhenium disulfide (ReS 2 ) stands out among them for its strong in-plane anisotropy and thickness-independent direct-bandgap excitons. These excitons can hybridize with light to form exciton–polaritons, rendering ReS 2 a compelling material for nanophotonic integration. Metasurfaces are arrays of subwavelength resonators and can support ultrasharp quasi-bound states in the continuum resonances. Topological transformations of their band structure can give rise to flatbands, which host dispersionless states with quenched kinetic energy and vanishing group velocity. Here we show that structuring ReS 2 into a resonant metasurface reshapes its photonic band topology, splitting the integer topological charge of the quasi-bound states in the continuum into two half-integer polarization singularities and driving the formation of directional far-field flatbands. Tuned into resonance with the linearly polarized excitonic transitions of ReS 2 , these flatband states hybridize into distinct directionally polarized exciton–polaritons. This points towards a scalable route to polarization-resolved quantum emitters, flatband-enhanced nonlinear optics and low-threshold polariton devices.

candidates.title: Glacial CO2 drawdown by plankton metabolic balance
candidates.authors: B. B. Cael, Malte F. Jansen, C. Mark Moore, Matthew B. Osman, Jamie D. Wilson
candidates.abstract: Which mechanisms caused the Holocene-versus-Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) difference? This longstanding question is crucial for characterizing glacial-interglacial cycles and using LGM climate information in climate predictions. We argue that the metabolic temperature dependence of epipelagic plankton is an important mechanism. Autotrophic plankton metabolisms are less sensitive to temperature than heterotrophic ones. Colder waters can thereby export and thus sequester more carbon in the deep ocean. We develop a theoretical model from Metabolic Theory of Ecology principles, then validate its predictions with empirical data compilations. We then use temperature reconstructions to estimate the plankton metabolism-driven LGM CO2 anomaly. Holding all other conditions at their pre-industrial state, such as net primary production and buffering capacity, we find that this mechanism represents a 6.2 ± 0.9ppm per degree global mean sea surface temperature change feedback, and can potentially explain 20 ± 5ppm, or ~ 1/4 of the total ~ 90ppm LGM CO2 anomaly. We diagnose a similar 18ppm using model data from an intermediate complexity Earth System Model that considers glacial-interglacial differences in nutrient limitation and primary production. Our findings are consistent with several temperature-driven mechanisms acting concertedly to modulate glacial-interglacial CO2 variations. In colder waters, plankton respiration slows down more than photosynthesis does, meaning more photosynthetically fixed carbon can sink to the deep ocean. It is estimated that this effect explains about a quarter of the CO2 drop during the last ice age.

candidates.title: Proximity labeling of the Listeria monocytogenes surface reveals pathogen control of a host deubiquitinase
candidates.authors: Patrick J. Woida, Maisie W. Smith, Rebecca L. Lamason
candidates.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes navigates a crowded intracellular environment by recruiting host factors to its surface in order to hijack the host actin cytoskeleton for motility and cell-to-cell spread. Although these types of Listeria-host interactions are critical for infection, systematic characterization of this interface has been limited. Here, we implement the biotin ligase split-TurboID to profile host proteins recruited to the surface of L. monocytogenes during intracellular infection. We show that the host deubiquitinase CYLD is enriched at the pathogen surface. While CYLD promotes infection by suppressing innate immunity in macrophages, how L. monocytogenes recruits and appropriates CYLD function in other cell types has remained unclear. We demonstrate that L. monocytogenes uses the secreted effector Internalin C (InlC) to redirect CYLD to M1-linked linear ubiquitin at the bacterial poles. Despite its localization, CYLD does not deubiquitinate bacteria or regulate autophagic clearance in epithelial cells. Instead, CYLD and InlC protect L. monocytogenes from IFN-γ- and RNF213-dependent restriction of cell-to-cell spread. Overall, our work profiling the bacterial surface-host interactome has identified a mechanism by which InlC spatially reprograms CYLD activity to promote cell-to-cell spread in epithelial cells. These findings highlight how L. monocytogenes exploits a host deubiquitinase to perform cell-type-specific functions during infection. The pathogen Listeria monocytogenes recruits host proteins to its surface within infected cells for motility and cell-to-cell spread. Here, Woida et al. adapt the split-TurboID technique to identify such proteins and show how a secreted effector co-opts a host deubiquitinase to counteract host restriction of bacterial spread.

candidates.abstract: Millions of synthesis procedures have been published, but their meta-analysis, important for identifying successful synthesis patterns, is difficult due to varied reporting structures. We present a simple, training-free workflow for laboratory action extraction that works across fields, encoding domain knowledge through explicit action sets and using powerful, readily available Large Language Models, or LLMs. Applied to zeolite synthesis, a widely used class of porous materials, our approach outperforms existing open-source tools and delivers context-aware results with open, locally runnable LLMs. It also matches state-of-the-art, field-specific models in their own domains, highlighting the generalization capabilities of current LLMs. The methodology showcased, along with the open algorithms made available, allow chemists to evaluate action sets, screen LLMs, and digitize laboratory procedures accurately with minimal effort. A domain-agnostic, training-free workflow leverages open-source large language models with explicit action sets and post-processing rules to extract laboratory procedures from unstructured text, demonstrated through zeolite synthesis.

candidates.abstract: Abstract When eukaryotic cells divide, a mitotic spindle, composed of microtubule filaments interacting with molecular motors, self-assembles and is responsible for aligning and segregating chromosomes to the opposite daughter cells. Recent structural studies revealed that spindles are composed of short microtubules that do not span the full pole-to-chromosome distance. It remains unclear how these short, disconnected microtubules collectively assemble a bipolar spindle. Using cryo-electron tomography to map microtubule polarity in human spindles, we find that microtubules organize with consistent 8 nm wall-to-wall spacing. Spacing scales inversely with local microtubule density, consistent with organization by density-driven steric interactions, analogous to liquid crystal ordering. We find that the Eg5 motor establishes local antiparallel overlap independently of spindle bipolarity, while a balance of Eg5 and dynein regulates microtubule density to maintain spindle architecture. Together, these findings reveal the mesoscale principles by which cells build complex, self-healing cellular architectures from nanoscale building blocks.

candidates.authors: Shuai Wu, Linwei Chen, Yunxiang Fu, Xiaoman Zhang, Luyang Luo, Meng Lou, Yangxi Huang, Guanhua Chen, Ying Fu, Ya Xing Wang, Qian Di, Yuyin Zhou, Xiang Li, Tien Yin Wong, Yizhou Yu, Hong-Yu Zhou
candidates.abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) offer potential advantages for clinical diagnosis over standard large language models (LLMs), yet their utility and safety remain unclear. Here we show, on AIMS-LDR, a long-context diagnostic reasoning benchmark built upon real-world electronic health records, covering six matched model pairs and 12 specialties, that LRMs generate over 34% more false positive diagnoses and show approximately 40% lower reproducibility than their LLM counterparts, while making more accurate primary diagnoses and more clinically relevant differentials. Experiments confirm this trade-off across prompt designs, model hyperparameters, and evaluation paradigms. A structured collaboration model, in which the LRM broadens diagnostic coverage and the clinician verifies reliability, increases diagnostic accuracy by 20% and reduces false positives by 44% in a 15-physician validation study. These results, obtained under controlled retrospective conditions, suggest that pairing LRM reasoning with physician oversight may support safer and more accurate diagnostic decision-making, warranting prospective validation before clinical deployment. This study finds that reasoning-enabled AI models improve diagnostic accuracy but produce more false positives and less consistent outputs but physician oversight helps retain benefits while reducing safety risks.

candidates.abstract: The rapid evolution of spermatogenesis limits the utility of mouse models for studying human spermatogenesis because some genes are absent or divergent in mice. Here we integrate histology and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from human, rhesus macaque, mouse and tree shrew testes to assess the tree shrew as a model of human spermatogenesis. We show that transcriptional landscapes in tree shrew spermatogenic cells, particularly late-stage spermatids, more closely resemble those of primates than mice. Conservation and enrichment analyses identify two core gene modules shared among humans, macaques and tree shrews but distinct in mice. Gene expression trajectories also align between tree shrews and primates, including for genes without murine orthologs. Immunostaining and RNA-FISH support representative expression patterns. These findings define contexts in which tree shrews can complement existing models of human spermatogenesis and male infertility. By comparing testis cell development across four mammals, this study shows that tree shrews more closely resemble primates than mice in key stages of sperm formation, supporting their use as a complementary model of human male fertility.

candidates.abstract: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is a mucosal yeast infection, mostly caused by Candida albicans, where symptoms are driven by inflammation. The onset of VVC is instigated by C. albicans pathogenicity, but the underlying causes of disease-driving hyperinflammation remain incompletely resolved. These albumin levels correlated with inflammatory cytokines in vaginal lavages. While the abundance of this serum protein in the vagina can be a hallmark of inflammation-induced vascular permeability, we reveal molecular mechanisms by which albumin can also drive inflammation. Albumin increased NLRP3 inflammasome activation in human macrophages elicited by C. albicans. This was associated with increased resistance of C. albicans to macrophage-mediated clearance in the presence of albumin. Further, albumin increased the expression of fungal secreted aspartic protease 1, which we identified as the effector driving inflammasome activation and IL-1β responses in vitro and in an in vivo VVC model. Moreover, neutrophils also exhibited impaired clearance of C. albicans in the presence of albumin. Collectively, vaginal albumin may not only be a consequence of inflammation of the vaginal mucosa, but also can drive C. albicans-induced hyperinflammatory IL-1β responses that underlie immunopathology in VVC. This study shows that high vaginal albumin in vulvovaginal candidiasis is not merely a correlate of inflammation, but can drive dysfunctional hyperinflammation by promoting fungal induced inflammasome activation, while compromising fungal clearance.

candidates.authors: Lun Gao, Xiaoman Lu, Weston Anderson, Corey Lesk, Elise Mazur, Fred Stolle, Peter Potapov, Francesco N. Tubiello, Steffen Fritz, Jiafu Mao, Liangzhi You, Deepak Ray
candidates.abstract: Arable land extent has undergone widespread changes across many regions worldwide through processes such as urban encroachment, forest conversion to agriculture, and dryland farming expansion. Using our self-developed arable land product integrated with global human settlement layers, Köppen–Geiger climate classifications, and historical land-use reconstructions, we show that the disproportionate climatic co-location of arable land and human settlements fundamentally structures global arable land dynamics. In contrast, low-latitude tropical regions continue to expand both systems at the expense of natural landscapes, partly driven by agricultural investment from Northern Hemisphere. Globally, these contrasting trajectories reveal a broader redistribution of agricultural pressure from climatically favorable regions toward less-exploited tropical and arid environments, linking settlement expansion and agricultural displacement to diverse environmental consequences including deforestation, biodiversity loss, groundwater depletion, and vegetation greening. These findings highlight the need to consider both local settlement–agriculture competition and broader agricultural redistribution when planning future food production and settlement growth. Arable land is changing through urban encroachment, forest conversion and dryland expansion, but these shifts are often viewed separately. The study demonstrates a unifying framework for global arable land redistribution and its environmental consequences.

candidates.authors: Xingxing Zhong, Mian Wei, Jing-Kai Wang, Yuqing Zhang, Xiaoyan Jiang, Jianhua Yu, Xiang Zhao
candidates.abstract: Abstract The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform—the partitioned- acs (pacs) net—has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D 2h ligands with lower-symmetry C 2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned- acs ), with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ) 1/3 . The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C 2 H 2 /CO 2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg −1 vs 0.98 mol kg −1 ).

candidates.authors: Trent Hall, Andrew Schild, Lei Li, Heather Sheppard, Hannah Chasteen, Yutian Liu, Anitria Cotton, Rashid Mehmood, Felipe Segato Dezem, Jason Hodges, Matthew Lear, Bailey Fountain, Yiping Fan, Jeffrey Gossett, Guolian Kang, Gabriela Gheorghe, Jeremy Chase Crawford, Paul Thomas, Yongqiang Feng, Gang Wu, Jasmine Plummer, Umar Boston, John D. candidates.abstract: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) have an elevated risk of autoimmune disease, particularly celiac disease, type 1 diabetes, and autoimmune hypothyroidism. In DS, thymi show characteristic structural and cellular changes, but the connection between these and the propensity to autoimmune disease is still unclear. Here we present a cell atlas from single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics of age-matched thymi from infants with and without DS, which might contribute to filling this knowledge gap. DS does not significantly alter CD34+ diversity in the thymus; however, the gene expression changes we observe indicate altered differentiative potential in DS CD34+ cells. Although many genes involved in T-cell development and function (including USP16, RUNX1 and ETS2) are located on chromosome 21, several important T cell regulatory genes that are located on other chromosomes also change in DS. In contrast, CD34- DS thymocytes are characterised by maturation defects. CD34+ progenitors and proliferating DP thymocytes are in a functional state of chronic interferon activation. In summary, we identify several notable differences in key functional cellular subsets and pathways within the DS thymus, providing insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of the thymic environment for this genetic condition. Down syndrome is a complex condition which results in immune alterations, including higher risk of autoimmune diseases. Here the authors show by single cell and spatial transcriptomics that the differentiation of thymic T cell precursors is disturbed in Down syndrome, which might underpin the functional alterations.

candidates.title: Deuteration of arenes in D2O exclusively driven by single-atom Pt sites under visible light
candidates.authors: Jie Xu, Xin-Yuan Wu, Rui Cao, Da Zhao, Xi-Zhong Song, Huan Chen, Wen-Wei Li, Tingrui Pan, K. M. Liew, Flemming Besenbacher, Yi-Tao Dai
candidates.abstract: Deuterated arenes play crucial roles in medicinal chemistry and materials science (e.g., psychotropic drugs and deuterated OLEDs). However, the desired late-stage deuteration via conventional hydrogen isotope exchange methods always demands expensive isotopic reagents (e.g., D2, C6D6, or C2H5OD), metal complex catalysts, or harsh conditions ( ≥ 120 oC, 20 bar H2). Here, we report a single-atom photocatalytic strategy for efficient deuteration of electron-rich arenes using D2O as the deuterium source. Under visible light irradiation at ambient temperature in an inert atmosphere, a single-atom photocatalyst (Pt1/TiO2) affords high deuterium incorporation across 54 electron-rich arene substrates. The protocol is mild, sustainable, and scalable: gram-scale synthesis of deuterated arenes (11.98 g, 100 mmol) was successfully realized. Mechanistic studies indicate that the catalytically active sites are primarily Pt–O coordinate bonds, whose light-modulated charge distribution facilitates a possible electrophilic platinization pathway for C–H activation before H/D exchange. Deuterated arenes are valuable in medicinal chemistry and materials science, but conventional hydrogen isotope exchange often requires costly reagents, metal complex catalysts or harsh conditions. Here, the authors report a single-atom photocatalytic strategy using D₂O as the sole deuterium source to efficiently deuterate electron-rich arenes under mild, scalable conditions.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Antibiotic resistance is a global health threat requiring antimicrobials with alternative modes of action. Growing evidence indicates that bacteria organize key intracellular processes through biomolecular condensates and other forms of spatial organization, yet whether such spatial organization can be exploited as an antimicrobial target remains unclear. Here, we identify intrinsically disordered antimicrobial peptides, generated from the Drosophila sleep-inducing protein Nemuri, that inhibit bacterial growth by targeting ribosomal organization. Mechanistically, these peptides enter bacterial cells without overt membrane disruption and accumulate in ribosome-rich regions, where they bind broadly to RNA and ribosomal surfaces through multivalent interactions. This engagement remodels ribosome-rich regions into condensates with reduced ribosomal mobility, thereby suppressing global protein synthesis and distinguishing these peptides from canonical site-specific ribosome-targeting antibiotics. Furthermore, Nemuri-derived peptides exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including activity against drug-resistant pathogens, with low cytotoxicity toward Drosophila and mammalian cells. Together, our findings identify the organization and material dynamics of bacterial ribosomes as a biophysical vulnerability that can be exploited by antimicrobial peptides, revealing how a naturally evolved metazoan host-defense system turns intracellular organization itself into an antibacterial target.

candidates.title: Widespread selection of antibiotic resistance within hospital sewers
candidates.authors: Declan A. Gray, Nguyen Thi Nhung, Roelof Dirk Coertze, Mutshiene Deogratias Ekwanzala, Noel Waters, Josef D. Järhult, Michaela Wenzel, Christina Åhrén, Jerker Fick, Carl-Fredrik Flach, D. G. Joakim Larsson
candidates.abstract: Abstract Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Hospital sewers contain more antibiotics than most environments and are thus increasingly recognised as potential arenas for resistance evolution. However, it is unknown if resistance selection occurs there and what the drivers are. Here we show selection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria within Swedish hospital sewers. Evidence include; consistent selection of multiple resistances in Escherichia coli exposed to filtered wastewater from ten hospitals, but not to corresponding municipal wastewaters; in-situ enrichment of resistant over sensitive E. coli from wastewater to sewer biofilms at hospitals, but not at municipal sites; and higher resistance in bacteria collected from hospital sewers than from municipal sites as assessed by culturing and metagenomics. Evidence for drivers includes complete rescue of sensitive E. coli by addition of resistance genes to fluoroquinolones and β-lactams, and cellular effects typical for β-lactams. Measured concentrations by liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry compared to selective thresholds identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as principal selective agents. Antibiotic concentrations and use data allow extrapolation of risks beyond Sweden. Given the absence of detectable selection at municipal sites, mitigations of risks in hospital sewers should be prioritized.

candidates.title: Layer-wise Prediction for Interpretation of Hidden Representations in Deep Neural Networks through Evolving Probability Distributions
candidates.authors: Zitu Liu, Yue Liu, Jiawang Li, Zhenyao Yu, Zhengwei Yang, Yike Guo, Qun Liu, Guoyin Wang
candidates.abstract: The sequential architecture of DNNs enables accurate predictions by encoding input features, yet their limited interpretability and transparency during forward propagation undermine the credibility of predictions. Therefore, we propose layer-wise prediction for interpretation method (LPI), which involves mapping the representation from each layer to a probability distribution, explaining the hidden-layer prediction process. To ensure interpretation fidelity to DNN mechanisms, we employ a reconstruction strategy to map probability distributions back to hidden layer features while reducing their influence on model prediction. Meanwhile, we define a rank-index metric to quantify the consistency of probability distribution evolution. Furthermore, we show how each hidden layer probability distribution evolves consistently during DNN forward propagation. Experiments on various models show that LPI achieves superior performance in consistency, stability, fidelity and certainty, outperforming AdditionalLayer, SDN, MetaGF, and DFS. Notably, LPI not only enhances deep learning interpretability but also provides valuable insights into reliable and credible model security assessment. Here, the authors introduce a hidden-layer interpretation method that maps intermediate DNN representations to probability distributions and reconstructs features to ensure faithful explanation.

candidates.title: Resolving the Kay–Dunn limit and the speed–endurance dilemma in ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 for DRAM-class sub-volt capacitors
candidates.authors: Geun Hyeong Park, Sanghyun Jo, Sungwook Park, Yong Hyeon Cho, Hyeong Seok Choi, Hyun Woo Jeong, Se Hyun Kim, Dong Hyun Lee, Moonseek Jeong, Taegyu Kwon, Da Hyun Kim, Ga Yeon Lee, Seunghwa Jeong, Young Yong Kim, Su Yong Lee, Younghwan Lee, Joonsuk Park, Chang Hwa Jung, Hanjin Lim, Daewoong Kwon, Ho Jun Kim, Min Hyuk Park
candidates.abstract: Abstract Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide can increase charge density in scaled capacitors, but its high coercive field limits the low-voltage, high endurance switching required for dynamic random-access memory and embedded ferroelectric memories. Here we show that plasma-engineered (111)-textured TiN electrodes with N-rich, oxidation-resistant surfaces suppress interfacial oxidation and enable robust switching in 5 nm Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 capacitors. The devices exhibit saturated hysteresis at 0.6 V, with 2 P r = 31.5 μC cm −2 and E c = 0.62 MV cm −1 , and no hard electrical breakdown through 10 12 bipolar cycles. Their nucleation-limited switching kinetics extrapolate to sub-nanosecond polarisation reversal at DRAM-relevant capacitor areas. At 1.1 V, circuit simulations of a common plate 1T–1 C cell yield short- and long-term stand-by sensing margins of 482 and 201 mV under a 20 fF bit line load. Electrode texture and interface engineering therefore enable low-voltage, high speed switching without compromising endurance, mitigating the practical Kay–Dunn scaling penalty and the speed–endurance dilemma.

candidates.authors: Liping Liu, Tianlai Xia, Rachel K. O’Reilly, Shichang Chen, Zaizai Tong
candidates.abstract: Polymer lamellar crystals commonly consisting of folded chains are frequently formed since they are kinetically favorable. Hence, the metastability of polymer crystals can be regulated by crystallization pathways, and the thinner lamellar crystals display a tendency to transform into thicker crystals via lamellar thickening process. Herein, we report that photoresponsive two-dimensional (2D) platelets with low metastability undergo controllable fragmentation upon light irradiation. Mechanistic studies indicate that the metastability within a single platelet particle is heterogeneous across different domains. Light irradiation triggers lamellar thickening preferentially within less stable domains decorated with photoresponsive molecules, leading to site-specific fragmentation. To illustrate the utility of light-stimulated fragmentation, wavelength selective fragmentation of 2D segmented platelets with spatially defined photoresponsive molecules is achieved upon light irradiation, yielding 2D hollow platelet structure. This important feature holds significant promise for advanced applications such as spatially resolved therapeutic delivery systems, thereby broadening the functional scope of 2D nanomaterials. Two-dimensional platelets are typically formed from polymer lamellar crystals, with metastability regulated by crystallization pathways. Here, the authors report photoresponsive platelets with low metastability, which undergo controllable fragmentation on light irradiation.

candidates.title: Increasing prevalence and expanding diversity of tet(X4)-carrying Salmonella in China
candidates.authors: Weiwei Li, Tingting Yang, Qingpo Cui, Baisheng Li, Li Zhan, Xiaotong Jiang, Shaofei Yan, Lu Liu, Xiaoxia Qin, Zhihong Liu, Luyu Ying, Bo Yu, Xin Qiao, Xiang Huo, Meng Zhang, Weiwei Chen, Xin Lu, Yunchang Guo, Mengjiao Fu, Zhangqi Shen
candidates.abstract: The plasmid-mediated tigecycline resistance gene tet(X4) threatens the efficacy of tigecycline. While prevalent in Escherichia coli across diverse ecological niches, its evolutionary trajectory in Salmonella remains underappreciated. Here, we conducted nationwide genomic surveillance of 42403 clinical nontyphoidal Salmonella isolates collected from diarrheal patients in China between 2014 and 2025, of which 102 were tet(X4)-positive. Although the overall prevalence remained low, detection showed a statistically significant upward trend over 2019-2025. Importantly, the newly accrued 2025 data were broadly consistent with short-term forecasts generated by the beta regression model, providing partial support for short-term trend consistency. Genomic analyses showed that tet(X4) remained concentrated in ST34 but was also detected in additional sequence types, including ST469, ST8971, ST11 and one isolate with an unassigned ST, across multiple provinces, indicating broader geographic representation and genetic diversification. Plasmid analyses likewise revealed broader replicon diversity, with the dominant IncHI1A/IncHI1B/IncFIA background accompanied by less frequent IncHI2/IncHI2A, IncI1(Alpha) and IncFIA/IncFIB/IncFIC. Phylogenetic analyses further revealed shared clustering of the dominant plasmid background across host species and bacterial genera, consistent with cross-host and cross-genus circulation. Here, they determine that tet(X4)-carrying Salmonella remains rare in China but is being detected more often and in a wider range of bacterial sequence types and plasmids, supporting continued surveillance.

candidates.abstract: Cresols are important urban emissions that can form multiple oxygen containing condensable vapors when they react with OH radicals in the atmosphere. These molecules contribute to secondary organic aerosols that have strong implications on climate and human health. In this work, we present flow reactor oxidation experiments demonstrating the rapid (sub-second) formation of condensable vapors with up to 10 oxygen atoms from the three cresol isomers (ortho-, para- and meta-cresol) under atmospheric conditions. Our quantum chemical calculations reveal that initial OH additions to the hydroxyl containing carbon atom lead to geminal diol intermediates that are critical to the rapid formation of condensable vapors from cresols and their key oxidation product, 3-methylcatechol. Incorporating these autoxidation mechanisms into model simulations shows that they contribute significantly to secondary organic aerosol composition. These results could explain the strong multi-generational contributions to aerosol from toluene and cresol, enabling a more accurate assessment of their climate and health impacts. Cresols and their oxidation products contribute to secondary organic aerosol, but their role in atmospheric oxidation remains poorly quantified. The authors report rapid formation of highly oxygenated organic molecules from cresols, identifying autoxidation mechanisms that could explain substantial multi-generational contributions to toluene and cresol secondary organic aerosol.

candidates.authors: Kaden Muffett, Stephen Williams, Sophia MacVittie, Mara JW Schwiesow, Susan Arechiga Mendoza, Salma Arechiga Mendoza, Hailey Hatch-West, E. Maggie Sogin
candidates.abstract: Abstract Acute and chronic exposure to elevated temperatures associated with Global Climate Change (GCC) threatens the structure and function of host-associated microbiomes, yet predicting microbial responses to heat stress remains challenging. We exposed two lines of the sea anemone, Exaiptasia diaphana , to acute and chronic thermal stress to quantify the impacts on cnidarian physiology and microbiome composition. Acute exposure caused rapid algal bleaching that was paired with pronounced shifts in bacteriome structure in both lines within 14 days of thermal exposure. Chronic exposure significantly affected the population structure, photo-physiology and bacteriome composition in only one host line, suggesting acclimation capacity depends on host-algal genetic backgrounds. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of 493 individuals sampled across 180 days, we found that sampling date explained nine-fold more variation in the microbiome composition than temperature exposure. Despite this temporal variation, we identified 16 indicator taxa that consistently changed in relative abundance under thermal stress. These taxa became central hubs in microbial association networks with increasing levels of thermal stress, suggesting they played key roles in bacteriome reorganization. As many of these taxa were present in other cnidarians, including reef-building corals, they may represent targets for conservation strategies that aim to enhance resilience on reefs.

candidates.title: LytU is a bridge-link isopeptidase that contributes to vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus
candidates.authors: Lina Antenucci, Chandan Thapa, Salla Virtanen, Timo A. Lehti, Annsy Arredondo, Ilona Pitkänen, Benita Westerlund-Wikström, Helena Tossavainen, Perttu Permi
candidates.abstract: Abstract Emergence of antimicrobial resistance is a pressing global issue. Although myriads of mechanisms for survival against antimicrobial pressure have surfaced, one key strategy is the structural modification of peptidoglycan, the main defense line in Gram-positive bacteria e.g., notorious pathogen Staphylococcus aureus . Here we show that the recently identified peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) LytU is an unusual catalyst in the lysostaphin (M23B) family of zinc-endopeptidases that hydrolyze the glycyl-glycine peptide bond in S. aureus . Unlike any other PGH recognized thus far, LytU hydrolyzes the isopeptide bond between the lysine ε amino group and pentaglycine, thus functioning as a bridge-link hydrolase. We discovered that LytM and LytU are functionally non-redundant, and they contribute to the cell wall remodeling at different stages of PG maturation. Additionally, we demonstrate that LytU particularly targets the PG precursor, pGly-Lipid II, and its overexpression leads to growth inhibition and a less densely cross-linked cell wall, which increases susceptibility to lysostaphin. Interestingly, LytU expression enhances resistance to the glycopeptide vancomycin, the drug of last resort against S. aureus .

candidates.abstract: Abstract Perovskite solar cells approach crystalline-silicon efficiencies at small areas, yet substantial performance losses during scale-up hinder their translation into practical modules. Here we quantify the contributions of device-performance parameters to efficiency loss during scale-up across diverse perovskite technologies, identifying fill factor ( $${FF}$$ F F ) as a major contributor and target for mitigating this loss. Further analysis resolves the FF deficit into voltage-, diode-non-ideality- and transport-associated contributions. Cryo-controlled processing provides an experimental route to preserve $${FF}$$ F F by regulating intermediate-phase evolution during crystallization. The resulting $${FF}$$ F F -preservation advantage arises predominantly from reduced diode non-ideality, with the other contributions being smaller. This advantage increases across device scales. A mini-module (19.48 cm 2 aperture) achieves a record certified steady-state efficiency of 23.9% with an $${FF}$$ F F of 83.3%, the highest reported for perovskite modules. The same $${FF}$$ F F limitation governs operational performance decay, linking efficiency retention during scale-up with long-term stability. Together, these results establish $${FF}$$ F F preservation and the factors governing it as central to mitigating performance loss during scale-up and operation.

candidates.title: Quantum Monte Carlo Studies of U(1) Lattice Gauge Models of Kondo Breakdown
candidates.authors: Gaopei Pan, Fakher F. Assaad
candidates.abstract: In the local-moment regime, heavy fermions are most economically described by a compact U(1) gauge theory. Motivated by this perspective, we study a minimal compact U(1) lattice gauge model describing a spin chain coupled to two-dimensional Dirac conduction electrons. The spin chain is described by fermionic partons carrying spin and U(1) gauge charge. The heavy-fermion quasiparticle is a bound state of a U(1) matter field carrying unit electric charge and U(1) gauge charge, and the fermionic parton. Using sign-problem-free determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we identify two symmetry-equivalent regimes: a heavy-fermion metal with a sharp composite-fermion resonance and robust low-frequency transport, and a Kondo-breakdown metal with an incoherent resonance and vanishing low-frequency transport. For any finite lattice extent in the direction perpendicular to the chain, the Luttinger volume of the heavy-fermion phase counts both composite and conduction electrons, while in the Kondo-breakdown phase it counts only the conduction electrons. The evolution of the composite-fermion spectrum, dynamical spin structure factor, and optical conductivity provides a nonperturbative demonstration of gauge-mediated Kondo breakdown and establishes transport fingerprints of an orbital-selective Mott transition in the context of U(1) gauge theories of heavy fermions.

candidates.abstract: Power-law eigenvalue spectra of covariance matrices estimated from data appear in diverse domains ranging from neural populations to proteins. We introduce a generative latent feature model for such data, optionally corrupted by measurement noise, and develop its spectral theory. We derive closed leading-order self-consistent equations for the Stieltjes transform of the covariance matrix from which the bulk eigenvalue density is obtained and provide a variational principle for the self-consistent equations. We also compute the positions and fluctuations of isolated top eigenvalues. The theory is validated in known algebraic limits and tested against simulations.

candidates.abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) near the first magic angle ($θ\approx1.05^{\circ}$) hosts flat bands that provide a fertile ground for exploring strongly correlated and topological phases. At smaller twist angles ($θ<1^{\circ}$), attice relaxation profoundly alters the moiré landscape. The extent to which moiré lattice reconstruction at different length scales affects the electronic structure through electro-mechanical coupling remains unresolved. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy on small-angle TBG devices ($θ\approx0.3-0.7^{\circ}$), we observe a pronounced $dI/dV$ peak at the AA site of the moiré lattice on top of a spectrum that is asymmetric about the charge neutrality point, lattice reconstruction over moiré lattice length scales, as well as a dilation of the atomic lattice at the AA sites. We demonstrate at a phenomenological level that the inclusion of moiré lattice reconstruction supports compact localized heavy fermion $f-$ states localized at AA sites. The additional inclusion of atomic lattice dilation enerates a strong flexo-electric response that explicitly breaks particle-hole symmetry, pushing compact, localized $f$-states at the AA sites down in energy. Consequently, these heavy fermion states energetically coexist with itinerant $c$-electrons at the AB/BA sites. Our spatially resolved spectroscopic measurements quantitatively visualize this coexistence, confirming the persistence of the heavy fermion model in the small-angle regime $θ<1^{\circ}$. Our findings provide microscopic insights into how flexo-electricity affects the low-energy electronic structure of small-angle TBG. More broadly, our study establishes small-angle TBG as a new class of moiré materials to explore the interacting Kondo lattice problem with high tunability of the $f-$occupation and $c-$density through twist-angle and electrostatic back gates, respectively.

candidates.abstract: Fully compensated ferrimagnets, characterized by nearly vanishing magnetic moments at zero temperature, perfect spin-polarized electronic structures, and ultrafast spin dynamics, represent a highly promising materials platform for next-generation spintronic devices. By minimizing stray magnetic fields and reducing switching currents, FCFs enable a viable path toward high-speed, low-power spintronic devices. In this work, we present a systematic investigation of the electronic structure, finite-temperature magnetism, and spin-dependent transport properties of the Heusler-type fully compensated half-metallic ferrimagnet Mn3Al in magnetic tunnel junctions. We demonstrate that Mn3Al is a half-metallic FCF with 100% spin polarization and fully compensated magnetization at 0 K. Combining density functional theory with Monte Carlo simulations, we characterize its finite-temperature magnetic properties and show that Mn3Al exhibits a net magnetization below 11.6 emu/cc at 300 K, confirming the robustness of its nearly compensated ferrimagnetic order at room temperature. Furthermore, we predict that the Mn3Al/MgO/Mn3Al MTJ yields a giant tunneling magnetoresistance effect at 0 K, which remains as high as 232% at 300 K. Our results establish Mn3Al and related half-metallic FCFs as excellent candidates for magnetoresistance-based spintronic applications.

candidates.abstract: TiN thin films have received great attention in the field of superconducting quantum computing due to their low loss characteristics derived from stable chemical and thermal properties, as well as excellent electrical conductivity. In this study, TiN thin films with a thickness of 35 nm were epitaxially grown on MgO substrates using the DC reactive magnetron sputtering technique. The crystal structure, film thickness, and surface morphology of the thin films were characterized. The films exhibit a very flat surface with a root mean square roughness of only a few tenths of a nanometer. The influences of nitrogen ($N_2$) flow rate on the surface morphology, superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), residual resistivity ratio (RRR), normal-state resistivity ($ρ_n$), upper critical field, and superconducting dimensionality were investigated systematically. The experimental results show that the TiN film deposited with a $N_2$ flow rate of 1.5 sccm exhibits optimal performance, including the highest $T_c$ (4.93 K), the largest RRR, the lowest $ρ_n$, and the lowest slope of the out-of-film upper critical field near Tc. Moreover, it is found that the background vacuum inside the growth chamber has a significant impact on the superconducting properties of TiN films, and the degradation of vacuum degree can lead to the decrease of $T_c$. The upper critical field reveals a significant anisotropic feature. Importantly, the in-film upper critical field data demonstrates that the optimization of sample quality leads to deviation from two-dimensional superconducting behavior, which provides a new perspective on the influencing factors of superconducting dimensionality beyond the thickness of films. The present results provide useful references for a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between growth parameters and the superconducting properties of thin films.

candidates.abstract: Giant optical nonlinearities enable advanced materials control and bridge exotic light-matter phenomena to next-generation photonics. However, materials exhibiting strong higher-order optical nonlinearity beyond the second order are typically rare. Here, we report the discovery of a giant and ultrafast second-harmonic generation (SHG) in self-assembled polar skyrmions under mid-infrared excitations. The transient SHG intensity exhibits a distinctive power dependence originating from higher-order nonlinearity. More generally, we show that large higher-order nonlinearity emerges across diverse domain structures in polar superlattices. Phase-field simulations demonstrate a strong and periodic local permittivity variation within each polar texture at equilibrium, and further confirm the fast polarization oscillation in polar skyrmions with mid-infrared excitations. This intense local permittivity modulation can satisfy epsilon-near-zero conditions, unlocking dramatically enhanced nonlinear optical responses without photonic engineering. Consequently, the self-assembled polar topologies with strong inherent optical nonlinearity could establish a platform for quantum information processing and high-speed optical communications.

candidates.abstract: Thermal laser evaporation (TLE) is an emerging physical vapor deposition (PVD) technique that uses continuous-wave lasers to evaporate even the most refractory elements. The deposition and characterization of superconducting refractory elements are of interest to assess the quality of films deposited by TLE. Here, we report the deposition of niobium (Nb) on c-plane sapphire using a home-built TLE system equipped with a 1070 nm continuous-wave fiber laser. A deposition rate of 0.19 Å/s was achieved with 533 W of laser power focused to a diameter of approximately 500 $μ$m on a Nb target. A film with a thickness of $22.47 \pm 0.05$ nm and a root-mean-square (RMS) roughness of $0.23 \pm 0.02$ nm exhibited a room-temperature resistivity of $21.60 \pm 0.05$ $μΩ\mathrm{cm}$ and a residual-resistivity ratio (RRR) of 5.71. The superconducting transition temperature, $T_\mathrm{c}$, of the film was measured as 9.24 K, only 10 mK below the bulk value, with a transition width of 29 mK. Among films deposited without substrate heating, the electrical and superconducting properties of the present films meet or exceed those deposited by other techniques. This work contributes to the emerging consensus regarding TLE as a versatile PVD method for refractory elements and compounds.

candidates.abstract: Altermagnets are collinear magnets with zero net magnetization and spin-split electronic bands. Here, we explore whether altermagnetism can exhibit a discontinuous jump, a phenomenon we refer to as meta-altermagnetism. We show that meta-altermagnetism can emerge in 2D systems when magnetic-order-induced band reconstruction drives spin-split van Hove singularities (vHSs) across the Fermi level. Using mean-field theory for an extended $t$-$J$ model on a two-sublattice square lattice including anisotropic hopping integral, we find that a first-order meta-altermagnetic transition produces an intermediate altermagnetic regime with reduced staggered magnetization but strongly enhanced magnetic octupole and time-reversal-odd spin-splitter conductivity. We further show that the first-order transition line terminates at a quantum critical endpoint, giving rise to a rich phase diagram as the chemical potential and anisotropic hopping strength are varied. Our results identify the spin split vHSs as a route to enhancing spin-splitter effect for spintronic applications.

candidates.abstract: Using numerically exact finite-temperature quantum Monte Carlo, we demonstrate that a $B_{1g}$ phonon coupled to the doped $t$-$t'$ repulsive Hubbard model produces genuine $d$-wave superconductivity at a substantial transition temperature, in excess of either interaction alone. The observed trends suggest that stronger Hubbard repulsion may cooperate with the phonon to further raise the pairing scale. The enhancement persists at stronger repulsion within the accessible window, limited by the fermion sign problem, and follows a common trend across phonon frequencies $Ω$ when organized by a retardation scale $2πT/Ω$. We also find a well-defined superconducting dome in doping, echoing a characteristic feature of correlated superconductors. Our results identify the $B_{1g}$ phonon as a plausible microscopic ingredient for robust $d$-wave superconductivity in the Hubbard model and suggest a concrete, physically motivated route toward materials with higher superconducting transition temperatures.

candidates.abstract: In this work we explore the complex magnetic behaviour of SrMnO3/La0.7Sr0.3MnO3/SrMnO3 trilayers combining magneto-optic Kerr effect (MOKE) and magneto-resistance measurements. The interplay of structural and orbital reconstruction and the competition of ferromagnetism/antiferromagnetism at the interfaces is responsible of a variety of complex magnetic properties, highlighting the use of heterostructures as an effective strategy to tune and control magnetic behaviour. We demonstrate the possibility to tune the magnetic properties of a ferromagnetic La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 (LSMO) layer, embedded in two homometallic antiferromagnetic layers (SrMnO3, SMO), by properly varying the role of interfaces using two different LSMO thickness values. Spin reorientation of the LSMO magnetic easy axis away from its room temperature orientation was observed below 125 K, due to the predominance of exchange interaction at the interface over the substrate-induced magnetic anisotropy, in agreement with established models for homometallic manganite heterostructures. The competition of super-exchange and exchange interactions at the interface results in a highly frustrated interfacial spin glass state, resulting in 20-fold enhancement of the coercive field and exchange bias. The modification of the magnetocrystalline anisotropy driven by the interfacial effects leads to a change in the anisotropic magneto-resistance response of the system, which dominates the low temperature behaviour.

candidates.abstract: In a ballistic system, the anomalous dc Hall response generically depends on microscopic details, including the geometric embedding of the orbitals and the precise implementation of the measurement. Here, we consider the question under what circumstances the anomalous Hall conductivity can be regarded as an intrinsic property of a system. We show that the full dc Hall response $σ_{xy}^{\rm H}$ becomes embedding-independent in the presence of relaxation by impurity scattering, although the individual (intrinsic) band and (extrinsic) side-jump and anomalous-distribution contributions to the Hall conductivity separately remain embedding-dependent. We further derive a symmetry criterion for when the band term itself becomes embedding-independent, but argue that this alone neither identifies it with the full Hall conductivity $σ_{xy}^{\rm H}$, nor makes it a reliable approximation for $σ_{xy}^{\rm H}$. More broadly, our results establish embedding dependence as a diagnostic of whether a response coefficient represents a stationary intrinsic property of a material or retains sensitivity to measurement protocol.

candidates.abstract: Artificial spin ices are geometric arrangement of nanomagnets that exhibit reconfigurable magnetization states and GHz dynamics. Their investigation in the GHz regime is challenging because of the existence of multiple modes and the impact of magnetization deviations at the edges of the nanomagnets. A minimal model to capture such dynamics require three macrospins per nanomagnet, an approach that was implemented for generic artificial spin ices in the tool Gaenice. Here, we use the Gaenice framework to realize a relaxation method to stabilize magnetization states self-consistently, called GaeniceN. We implement the dissipative component of the Landau-Lifshitz equation in an iterative approach to efficiently converge to the relaxed state. As an example, we find our approach to correctly predict the transition between phases in a pyramid ASI subject to a low-magnitude external field by computing the system's average energy. Because they are rooted on the same framework, GaeniceN produces the initial condition needed for Gaenice to compute dynamics such as ferromagnetic resonance or band structures. Combined, these tools will be able to aid in the design of artificial spin ices with applications in magnonics.

candidates.abstract: Structural disorder can stabilize frameworks against pressure-induced failure, yet the ordered regions it contains limit this gain. We show that, in rigid-jointed frames under hydrostatic pressure, an ensemble containing arbitrarily large patches of a crystal at positive density, whose centres carry a scaled crystal prestress, cannot stay linearly stable once those patches are stressed beyond the crystal's threshold for localizable instabilities. A homogeneous loss of positive definiteness while all Bloch modes, including the acoustic limit, remain stable cannot localize, leaving a window for stabilization. Extending an acoustic criterion to prestress, we show for all point groups that such a window requires a strain that keeps the crystal's symmetry. Unless the patches are shielded from stress, disorder cannot protect a crystal against a failure that breaks its symmetry, and protects a cubic crystal at most against volume collapse. In two-dimensional Truchet frames, planted ordered domains bring the threshold within 1% of the bound, and correlations short of long-range order localize failure on ordered clusters. Across 876 slender-strut nets, 798 fail first by a localizable instability; the other 78 have a median window of 7.6%. Stability gained through disorder is capped by the localizable instabilities of the local order it permits.

candidates.abstract: Rare events and large-deviation theory have attracted considerable interest in the study of random walks. Here, we investigate the rare events of the positional distribution of continuous-time random walks under ordinary and equilibrium initial conditions using the saddle point method. We show that the far-tail behavior is sensitive to the expansion of the waiting-time distribution near its minimum value. For a general power-series expansion near the minimum waiting time, the positional distribution exhibits an approximately exponential decay in its far tails. In contrast, when the waiting-time distribution has a cutoff at its minimum value, the positional distribution exhibits an unexpected Gaussian decay, in contrast to the far-tail behavior of the renewal-count distribution. We further find that the most likely number of renewals required to reach a given position, as well as the associated rate functions, is insensitive to the initial conditions, whereas the far tails of the positional distribution retain a dependence on the initial conditions. Our results provide new insights into the rare-event statistics and large deviations of random walks.

candidates.abstract: Spatially resolved control of coherent electron transport offers a route to understanding and engineering interference phenomena in hybrid superconducting devices. Here, we use Scanning Gate Microscopy (SGM) to investigate Fabry-Pérot (FP) interference in the n-p-n cavity of a ballistic graphene Josephson junction. Spatial maps of the superconducting switching current and normal-state conductance reveal circular interference fringes arising from two distinct effects of the SGM tip potential. A global shift of the Fermi wave vector modulates the FP resonances of the cavity, while a local perturbation produces additional oscillations that persist at fixed Fermi wave vector as the tip bias is varied. An analytical model identifies the origin of this local response with coherent electron lensing, in which the tip modifies the phase accumulated along interfering trajectories. The measured fringe patterns in the switching current indicate that this mechanism affects superconducting transport, consistent with tip-induced shifts of the resonance conditions for Andreev bound states. These results establish SGM as a tunable local lens for controlling interference in superconducting ballistic graphene devices.

Static magnetization reveals competing antiferromagnetic exchange interactions of $J_1=-8.1(2)$ THz ($-33.5(8)$ meV) between the central and the peripheral sites and $J_2=-4.40(12)$ THz ($-18.2(5)$ meV) between neighboring sites on the ring of the metallacrown, which are corroborated by ab initio broken symmetry-based density functional theory (DFT). The ground-state spin-configuration is characterized by $d_{xy}$-character of the unoccupied states. Furthermore, our magnetization data evidence thermal transitions across a doublet-to-quartet gap of $Δ_{1/2\rightarrow3/2} = 4.8(4)$ THz which is also indicated by the emergence of an excited-state EPR signal.

We expand the cavity equations around the fully-connected mean-field limit, focusing on the critical behavior of the system: our approach allows us to compute the de Almeida-Thouless line of mean-field finitely-connected systems in the temperature $T$--magnetic field $H$ plane, by means of closed analytical equations. On the theoretical side, we are able to identify three sources of corrections to the fully-connected mean-field solution: i) the non-Gaussianity of the cavity fields, ii) the statistical correlation between the cavity fields and their fluctuations, and iii) the corrections to the cavity filter functions. These corrections are treated using two different expansions: a non-uniform expansion, where we expand all three contributions around the mean-field solution, and a uniform expansion, where we only expand the statistics but leave the cavity filters untouched. The former allows for a direct comparison with the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model but fails at low temperatures, as a consequence of the de Almeida-Thouless line diverging in the zero-temperature limit. On the other hand, the uniform expansion describes with good accuracy the critical behavior of the system. We also extend these results to the $T = 0$ limit.

candidates.abstract: We study the interacting Kitaev chain with nearest-neighbor interactions and finite chemical potential using a combination of bosonization and density-matrix renormalization-group calculations. Focusing away from special exactly solvable lattice limits, we develop a continuum field-theoretic description of the generic finite-density interacting regime, where doping nonperturbatively modifies the competition between superconducting pairing and commensurate charge ordering. We show that the phase diagram consists of an intermediate incommensurate Luttinger liquid between the topological superconducting and commensurate charge-density-wave Mott phases, as well as a trivial band-insulating regime at large chemical potential. The commensurate--incommensurate and incommensurate--topological-superconducting phase boundaries are governed by Pokrovsky--Talapov and Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless criticality, respectively. We analyze the interacting topological superconducting regime and its boundary excitations. At the semiclassical level, and explicitly in the free-fermion boundary theory, the topological phase supports exponentially localized Majorana edge modes at interfaces between topological and trivial regions. We also construct a dual continuum fermionic representation in which this topological bulk sector is described instead by conventional symmetry breaking. This gives a continuum version of the SPT--SSB correspondence between different fermionic representations. Overall, our results provide an analytical description of one-dimensional interacting topological superconductors, from the competition between topology and commensurability and the resulting quantum criticality to the dual symmetry-breaking description of the topological phase.

The validated model will serve as a robust baseline for extending this method to measure effective thermal conductivity as a function of the heater size. This approach is particularly relevant for materials where non-diffusive thermal transport regimes enable probing phonon MFP dependent contributions to the thermal conductivity.

We study prescribed nonequilibrium phonon pulses in a Majorana qubit formed by two $2\,μ\mathrm{m}$ proximitized nanowires. Combining the lattice Lutchyn--Oreg model, microscopic electron--phonon coupling, and parity-resolved many-body dynamics, we track excitation, relaxation, and logical coherence. Without quasiparticle escape, recombination restores the initial Majorana occupations in about 130 ns, while phonons exchanged during excitation and recovery can retain logical-state information, leaving permanent coherence loss. For mirror-symmetric wires, the fractional coherence loss per wire is 0.75--1.0 times the excitation probability averaged over the two logical states, even at zero Majorana splitting; breaking mirror symmetry can suppress dephasing at small splitting. Factorized Boltzmann kinetics neglects quasiparticle correlations and overestimates residual parity flips. At equal deposited energy density, phonon spectra yield different excitation probabilities and coherence losses. Comparisons with Kitaev chains matched to the wire's gap and Majorana decay length reveal that low electron density suppresses excitation by energetic phonons, whereas hard-wall boundaries in a high-density control increase excitation efficiency by a factor of $5\times10^4$ relative to the wire for pulses centered at 1 meV. Magnetic-field and chemical-potential tuning yield different phonon sensitivities at the same bulk gap through changes in spin and electron--hole structure. Including hybrid states' semiconductor weights reduces near-threshold excitation rates fourfold when the tunnel coupling equals the parent superconducting gap. Our framework connects phonon spectra to leakage, poisoning, and coherence loss to guide Majorana-device design.

candidates.abstract: Spin space groups provide a complete symmetry classification of magnetic structures in the non-relativistic limit and have become an increasingly useful language for organizing magnetic phases and their physical properties. Each spin space group with a given parent space group is specified, up to spin-only symmetries, by a real representation of that space group acting in spin space. We argue that working directly with this representation not only avoids the construction and identification of the group, but also organizes and simplifies the resulting symmetry constraints on allowed responses. Determining the presence or absence of magnetic compensation, piezomagnetism, spin and charge transport, the Edelstein effect, and momentum-space spin textures becomes an ordinary problem in the representation theory of space groups. The resulting conditions reduce to overlaps between the three exterior powers of the defining representation and multipole representations of the point group. Several physically distinct responses then reduce to the same condition on the defining representation. For example, a $p$-wave spin texture and the time-even Edelstein effect are allowed under the same condition, as are piezomagnetism and a $d$-wave spin texture in compensated order. The wave-vector content of the exterior powers gives a further hierarchy of selection rules: depending on the relevant power, a uniform response requires one, two, or three ordering wave vectors to sum to a reciprocal lattice vector. These rules can exclude many responses before point-group symmetry is considered. We illustrate the approach with examples drawn from a wide variety of materials hosting collinear, coplanar and non-coplanar magnetic order. Finally, we discuss extensions of these results to magnetic space groups, connections to Landau theories of collinear order, and the characterization of odd-parity magnets.

candidates.abstract: Floquet phenomena - where a coherent, time-periodic drive hybridizes the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band - have been demonstrated with intense optical fields and, more recently, other bosonic excitations. However, within mean-field approximations and the current understanding of Floquet phenomena, these effects survive only for the coherence time of the drive, limiting practical use and current demonstrations to the sub-picosecond regime. Here, consistent with recent theoretical predictions beyond the mean-field picture, using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy in WSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructures, we show that incoherent, dense populations of dark interlayer excitons hybridize the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band, mimicking Floquet-like phenomena - now persisting for nearly a nanosecond. With increasing interlayer exciton density, the valence band and its replica evolve from an inverted-parabolic to a Mexican-hat dispersion, a signature of the predicted non-zero static coupling that hybridizes the bands and scales linearly with the exciton density. By tuning twist angle, we further show that dark excitons with net momentum create replicas that hybridize with bands offset not just in energy but also in momentum, providing another powerful degree of freedom beyond conventional Floquet engineering. These results establish a robust, long-lived route to engineering electronic states, beyond a coherent, zero-momentum drive.

candidates.abstract: Transverse thermoelectric conversion, in which charge and heat currents are interconverted in orthogonal directions, has recently attracted increasing attention as an alternative to conventional longitudinal thermoelectric conversion. Although transverse Seebeck effect has been investigated in various materials, its reciprocal process, transverse Peltier effect, remains much less explored, and direct comparison of the two effects in the same homogeneous material is still limited. Here, we experimentally investigate both transverse Seebeck and Peltier effects in a single crystal of MoSi2, an axis-dependent conduction polarity material in which the sign of the Seebeck coefficient varies depending on the crystallographic axis. Multi-terminal voltage measurement determines the direction of the induced internal electric field and establishes the transverse Seebeck response. We also directly visualize the transverse temperature modulation consistent with the corresponding transverse Peltier effect by using lock-in thermography under an applied ac current. These results establish reciprocal transverse thermoelectric conversion in a homogeneous nonmagnetic single crystal without engineered interfaces.

candidates.abstract: Polymorphic transformations occur in a minority of metals. Tungsten is not one of them. This observation does not rule out its intrinsic phase transition possibility, but may be due to inaccessible thermodynamic and mechanical conditions in conventional experiments. Herein, we investigate the body centered cubic (BCC) to face centered cubic (FCC) transformation in tungsten via a rigorously validated machine learning potential (MLP) molecular dynamics (MD) approach. Our simulations demonstrate that strain induced BCC to FCC transformation indeed occurs in tungsten. The FCC phase exceeds 20 at.% at low temperature and in the presence of dislocations. In the perfect crystal moderate temperatures favor phase transformation kinetics. Structural analysis confirms the transformation following the Bain and Nishiyama Wassermann orientation relationship. These results establish the viability of strain induced polymorphic transformation in tungsten and provide a critical guideline for the experimental production of duplex tungsten with enhanced ductility addressing a longstanding challenge in tungsten material engineering for high-temperature structural applications.

candidates.abstract: The superconducting diode effect is often associated with finite-momentum pairing, although model studies indicate that rectification reflects the asymmetry of the free energy about its minimum rather than the equilibrium pair momentum itself. Using a Wannier-based, self-consistent finite-$\mathbf Q$ Bogoliubov-de Gennes approach with a Fermi-surface-adaptive quadrature that converges the critical currents, we show that the layer parity and orientation of magnetic proximity select the diode response of monolayer NbSe$_2$. For in-plane exchange, the equilibrium pair momentum $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}$ and the diode efficiency are both linear in the layer-odd exchange contrast: parallel proximity on the two Se sublayers is reciprocal, and antiparallel proximity doubles the response. An out-of-plane component separates the two observables. It leaves $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}$ nearly unchanged but, through pair breaking, suppresses the efficiency by more than an order of magnitude and, at low temperature, reverses it. Purely out-of-plane exchange, for which $C_3$ symmetry forbids a helical term, keeps $\mathbf Q_{\rm eq}=0$ yet produces a trigonal diode effect, controlled by the layer-even exchange and larger than the in-plane one above $0.65$~meV at low temperature. Magnetic layer parity thus selects between a helical and a trigonal diode channel. The trigonal channel is an intrinsic, symmetry-allowed contribution to the field-free rectification reported in NbSe$_2$/CrBr$_3$ and predicts that two-sided out-of-plane proximity cancels it when antiparallel and, at the same exchange per layer, enhances it about fourfold when parallel, in the computed range.

candidates.abstract: Tellurium dioxide (TeO$_2$) is a wide-bandgap oxide with attractive processing versatility and emerging p-type semiconducting behaviour, making it a promising material system for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications. However, TeO$_2$-derived thin films prepared by scalable manufacturing processes, such as vacuum sublimation, can contain residual metallic Te$^0$ species that introduce trap states, limit hole transport, and promote carrier recombination. Here, we demonstrate a selenium alloying strategy to control the defect chemistry of vacuum-sublimed TeO$_x$ films. TeO$_2$:Se powder mixtures (90:10~wt\%) were thermally evaporated and subsequently annealed in air at 225~$^\circ$C for up to 9~h, yielding amorphous TeO$_x$:Se films with an optical bandgap of 0.98~eV under optimised conditions. Structural, chemical, optical, and electrical analyses show that prolonged annealing promotes Se redistribution, suppresses residual Te$^0$ to approximately 0.4\%, reduces the film's surface roughness, and shifts the valence-band edge. To evaluate the potential of TeO$_x$:Se for photovoltaic applications, we fabricated thin-film solar cells with an ITO/ZnO/TeO$_x$:Se/MoO$_x$/Ag architecture. Devices based on an 80~nm TeO$_x$:Se active layer annealed for 9~h exhibit optimal performance, with broadband photocurrent generation from 300 to 1000~nm, yielding an open-circuit voltage of 0.50~V, a short-circuit current density of 8.50~mA~cm$^{-2}$, a fill factor of 0.44, and a maximum power conversion efficiency of approximately 1.87\%. These results establish selenium-alloyed TeO$_x$ as a viable oxide-derived absorber for thin-film photovoltaics and highlight chemical-state control as an effective route for improving photovoltaic performance.

We compare Wyckoff deformations of atomic configurations with symmetry-preserving adiabatic deformations of occupied states, both with and without adding common occupied atomic orbitals. Explicit examples show that stable Wyckoff equivalence and adiabatic equivalence at fixed filling do not imply each other. These groups preserve spacetime orientation and have a point whose site-symmetry group contains $222$, $\overline1'$, or $\overline4'$.

candidates.abstract: Identifying the key ingredients for superconductivity under pressure in the Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates remains a formidable challenge, due to a complex interplay between structural variations, oxygen content and location, electronically ordered phases, and the need for high pressures to reach the superconducting phase. To disentangle these complex inter-dependencies, here we study a series of clean single crystals of trilayer La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10}$. We discover that enhanced biaxial, compressive pressures induce a zero-resistance state at a 60\% lower pressure compared to previous reports. At the same time, we completely separate the low-pressure density wave phase from superconductivity, effectively ruling out that soft, quantum critical fluctuations of the density wave order parameter act as the pairing glue in this system. Our results establish biaxial, in-plane pressures as a powerful tool for promoting superconductivity in nickelates, unifying the required pressure scales for superconductivity in different Ruddlesden-Popper structures, and providing a connection to the recently discovered thin film samples.

candidates.abstract: Understanding how superconductivity emerges from correlated electronic states is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. The quasi-one-dimensional spin-ladder compound \bfs\ serves as a unique platform to study this interplay, as it lacks the two-dimensional square lattice characteristic of most iron-based superconductors. Here, we combine high-pressure x-ray and neutron diffraction, x-ray emission spectroscopy, and electrical transport to map its structural, magnetic, and electronic evolution into the superconducting regime. We \revised{observe} a striking pressure-induced decoupling: while the long-range stripe-type antiferromagnetic order remains remarkably robust under pressure up to the onset of superconductivity, the local iron magnetic moment is suppressed by nearly 80\%. This dichotomy \revised{points to an orbital-selective mechanism}, where specific Fe $3d$ electrons remain localized to sustain magnetism while others delocalize to form the itinerant and superconducting state. \revised{Superconductivity emerges while long-range magnetic order is still present, revealing that the two coexist in \bfs, which we attribute to} the selective response of multiorbital electronic degrees of freedom.

candidates.abstract: Friction and wear of diamond are controlled by its surface chemistry, which determines whether covalent bonds form across the sliding interface. First-principles simulations have explored the role of surface orientation and passivation, but are limited to a few hundred atoms and tens of picoseconds. To bridge this gap, we develop a reactive machine learning interatomic potential for the C/H/N/O/Si chemical space, covering diamond, silicon nitride, silicon oxide, their surfaces, interfaces, and environmental molecules. The potential is trained on a large dataset of diverse structures and is tested on multiple physical properties, including ab initio reaction barriers on diamond surfaces, and structural/mechanical properties of amorphous Si$_3$N$_4$ and SiO$_2$. We then simulate sliding of diamond-Si$_3$N$_4$ interfaces with four surface orientations, clean and H/OH-passivated terminations, and normal loads from 0.1 to 23 GPa. We identify two different regimes: one where sliding is localized at the interface, and shear stress is proportional to the interfacial bond density, and another where shear is distributed inside the softer material, and adhesion due to full interfacial bonding dominates. These results show how passivation, surface orientation and load together determine interfacial bonding and friction, with implications for the environmental sensitivity of diamond wear. candidates.abstract: The Gibbs states of local Hamiltonians have short-range conditional correlations. To maintain a steady state with long-range conditional correlations, one might expect that a stochastic process must ``pay'' either in nonlocal moves or entropy production. Surprisingly, we find strictly local Gaussian processes that obey detailed balance and have unique steady states with arbitrarily long-range conditional correlations. We show that such processes must still produce entropy, if implemented using a local quadratic Hamiltonian coupled locally to equilibrium, rapidly relaxing baths. We lower-bound this entropy production in terms of the steady state's conditional mutual information (CMI); if the CMI decays exponentially with distance, the associated length-scale is called the Markov length $ξ$. The entropy production per site per relaxation time obeys $\hatσ\ge c ξ^2$ for large $ξ$, and with $c$ an implementation-dependent constant. We also bound the tradeoff between coupling range and entropy production. We contrast these Gaussian processes with jump processes on discrete state spaces, for which, under certain irreducibility assumptions, steady states with long-range CMI are only possible if detailed balance is violated. We conjecture (and present evidence) that rapidly mixing local jump processes cannot stabilize steady states with long-range CMI.

candidates.abstract: Large language model agents have begun to carry out laboratory measurements, but their scientific conclusions are useful only if they hold up under scrutiny. Demonstrating this requires controlled studies because models are stochastic and the context a model is given steers its conclusions. Here we introduce HERA, an autonomous agent designed to carry out cryogenic transport measurements of quantum devices. HERA draws on a knowledge base curated by lab members that holds measurement protocols, software tools, and literature references. We assessed HERA with a blinded trial against an expert on the stacking order of two multilayer graphene devices, an ablation of its knowledge base, and hundreds of offline replays in which models designed the trial's central measurement without running it. HERA's conclusions matched the expert's sealed conclusions on both tested devices. The ablation and the replay studies measured the impact of the knowledge base across different models, showing that with it every model designed better measurements and reasoned more soundly. To test how readily HERA extends to a new problem, we tasked it with finding and characterizing superconductivity in a different material system. This required a few hours of expert time to develop a new experimental protocol, after which HERA did both autonomously. These results show that, with a knowledge base designed for the task, language model agents are capable of sound experimental science.

In the experiments, various double-well systems subjected to sinusoidal forces is explored, and the effects of both driving force and frequency is analyzed. Results reveal characteristic stochastic resonance behavior for weak drives and adiabatic manipulation at strong, low-frequency drives. Although our experimental method requires a steady sinusoidal drive incompatible with Landauer's erasure protocol, our numerical analysis demonstrates that the work required for such bit manipulation (erasure) is within an order of magnitude of Landauer's limit ($k_B T \ln 2$) at 4.2 K. These findings open possibilities for creating highly efficient memory elements that could be integrated with cryogenic quantum circuits or function as topological quantum computing qubits; thereby contributing to memory devices with lower energy consumption and mitigating the escalating global energy demand in the computing industry.
